To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the MAGIC stereoscopic system is able to measure the Crab Nebula differential flux with a 5 % systematic uncertainty in 1 decade of energy; 2) there is a hint of variability in the Crab Nebula flux on daily timescales at VHEs, but it is not significant when systematic uncertainties are taken into account; 3) the VHE spectral energy distribution can be reproduced with a 1D time-dependent model with a 80 μ G magnetic field, but

1) the MAGIC stereoscopic system is capable of providing a precise spectral determination of the Crab Nebular spectrum from 50 Gev to 30 TeV, 2) there is no indication of variability on daily time scales at energies above ∼ 300 GeV, 3) the spectral energy distribution can be well described by a time-dependent 1 D model, 4) a constant magnetic field model cannot reproduce the observed spectral energy distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for the best model to describe the overall spectrum and morphology of the Crab Nebular.
the question whether the current models are able to explain the observed VHE spectrum of the Crab Nebular.
the question of the origin of the broad Inverse Component peak.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VHE data are in agreement with the time-dependent 2D model, but this is only a qualitative statement, as the model has not been tuned to reproduce the VHE data.
the VHE spectral results presented in this work provide strong constraints to the theoretical models of the Crab Nebular, but do not yet allow us to choose one model over the others.
a single theoretical model cannot describe the whole spectrum of the Crab Nebular from radio to VHE gamma rays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can rule out the constant B-field model, but cannot rule out either of the two time-dependent spectral models.
the 1D model is not able to explain the observed VHE data.
the 3D time-dependent model is the only one able to describe the data, although the fit is not perfect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current theoretical models are not yet able to simultaneously describe the morphology and spectral energy distribution of this source, which is the key to understand the emission mechanisms at work in the nebula.
the new VHE spectral data can help to constrain theoretical models, which are otherwise underdetermined by lower energy data alone.
the VHE gamma-ray emission is not only produced in the inner region of the nebula.
